# Get started on mps2-an385 in QEMU (bare-metal)

<!-- type: how-to · level: 1 -->

**Needs first:** [Install](../start/install.md)

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED by scripts/gen-board-support.py: starter status -->
> **Status:** Verified in emulator (daily). From the board support registry: [`nros-board-mps2-an385`](../reference/boards/mps2-an385.md); [Board Support Levels](../reference/board-support-levels.md) explains the words.

This starter puts a Rust talker on an Arm Cortex-M3 board with no operating
system at all, emulated by QEMU, and shows its messages arriving in ROS 2. The
board is Arm's MPS2-AN385, which QEMU models closely. No one buys one: it is
the board this book teaches nano-ros on, because it costs nothing and behaves
like a real microcontroller. The talker runs as one loop with no scheduler
under it, which is what "bare-metal" means.

## What you need

- A Linux host with the [install](../start/install.md) done, so `nros` is on
  your `PATH`.
- ROS 2 Humble with `ros-humble-rmw-zenoh-cpp`. ROS 2 provides the zenoh
  router the board talks to, and the message definitions the build generates
  the talker's code from.

Nothing else: no board, no cable, no root access. The board talks to your
machine over its emulated serial port, the way a real board's first program
does. Its network comes later, under [Next](#next). WiFi is deferred to the
Zephyr 4.4 line, so no starter opens over WiFi yet.

## Provision

```bash probe=30
nros setup mps2-an385-baremetal --rmw zenoh
```

That fetches the Arm cross-compiler, the QEMU that emulates the board, and the
Rust `thumbv7m-none-eabi` target into a shared store under `~/.nros`. Nothing
is installed system-wide. It installs no router: the router is ROS's
`rmw_zenohd`.

## Scaffold the project

```bash probe=40
nros new bm_ws --board mps2-an385-baremetal --template talker --lang rust --rmw zenoh
cd bm_ws
```

That wrote a workspace with two packages:

```text
bm_ws/
└── src/
    ├── bm_node/                 # the talker: package.xml, Cargo.toml (a library), src/lib.rs
    └── bm_node_bringup/         # package.xml and system.toml: the board, the RMW, the node
```

`bm_node` is the talker, a library with no `main()` that names no board. It
publishes `std_msgs/String` on `/chatter` once a second. `bm_node_bringup`
says what the talker runs on. You do not need to open it for this starter.

## Run it in QEMU

Source ROS 2, then build and run. This first run records the ROS 2 prefix in
the workspace, so later runs of it need no sourced shell (the router still
comes from ROS 2):

```bash probe=50 probe-run=1500
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
nros run bm_node --expect 'Publishing:'
```

```text probe-expect=50
Publishing: 'Hello World: 1'
nros run: matched after
```

`nros run` builds the firmware (the first build compiles nano-ros for the
Cortex-M3 and takes about five minutes; later builds take seconds), boots it
in QEMU with the board's serial port connected to a terminal device on your
host, and starts the router on that device. What it prints is the board's
console. With `--expect` it stops everything and exits 0 at the first console
line containing that text, and exits 1 if the board stops first.

Without `--expect` it keeps running until you press Ctrl-C, which stops QEMU
and the router together. Start it that way in one terminal:

```bash probe=60 probe-run=300 probe-keep
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
nros run bm_node
```

```text probe-expect=60
Publishing: 'Hello World: 2'
```

## See it in ROS 2

Leave `nros run` going. In a second terminal:

```bash probe=70 probe-run=120
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
ros2 topic echo /chatter std_msgs/msg/String --qos-reliability best_effort
```

```text probe-expect=70
data: 'Hello World:
```

The talker publishes best-effort, and `ros2 topic echo` defaults to reliable,
which receives nothing from it. That is why the command asks for best-effort.
The router `nros run` started also listens where a ROS 2 node on this machine
looks for one, so nothing else needs to be configured.

## If it doesn't work

- **`nros run` stops at once and names `AMENT_PREFIX_PATH`:** this shell has
  not sourced ROS 2, and no earlier build of the workspace recorded it. Source
  it and run again.
- **`nros run` stops at once and names the router:** it could not find
  `rmw_zenohd`. Source ROS 2 in that shell, and install
  `ros-humble-rmw-zenoh-cpp` if it is missing.
- **No `Publishing:` line within a minute of boot:** the router started but
  the board did not reach it. `nros run` names the router's log under
  `build/nros/run/` when it stops. A router you started yourself on the same
  port is the usual cause.
- **The talker stalls after you change it:** bare-metal has no preemption, so
  a callback that runs long stops every other callback until it returns.
- **Everything else:** [Troubleshooting - First 10 Minutes](../reference/troubleshooting-index.md).
